mcqs.q: Under the classification of impression materials, the elastomers fall under:
mcqs.explain: The elastic group contains the hydrocolloids and the elastomers; impression plaster, wax, compound and ZOE are the rigid ones.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a RIGID impression material?
mcqs.explain: Impression plaster, impression wax and impression compound are the other three rigid materials.

mcqs.q: Which material sets by a PHYSICAL (reversible) reaction and is therefore thermoplastic?
mcqs.explain: Impression compound and impression wax are the rigid thermoplastics; agar is the elastic one.

mcqs.q: Impression plaster and zinc oxide-eugenol are used for:
opts: Impressions of edentulous ridges and interocclusal records
Impressions of prepared teeth for crowns
mcqs.explain: Being rigid, they cannot be withdrawn past undercuts, so they are restricted to edentulous ridges and bite records.

mcqs.q: The first synthetic elastomeric impression material, introduced in 1950, was:
mcqs.explain: Condensation silicones followed in 1955, polyethers in 1965 and addition silicones in 1975.

mcqs.q: Which elastomer was introduced MOST RECENTLY?
mcqs.explain: The order of introduction is polysulfide, condensation silicone, polyether, addition silicone.

mcqs.q: Elastomeric impression materials are covered by:
mcqs.explain: They are also known as non-aqueous elastomeric dental impression materials.

mcqs.q: The elastic behaviour of an elastomer is explained by the fact that:
opts: The chains uncoil on stretching and snap back to their entangled state
The material melts and resolidifies with each deformation
Water is absorbed and released from the matrix
The filler particles slide over one another
mcqs.explain: The molecules have weak interaction among them but are tied together at certain points to form a three-dimensional network.

mcqs.q: All elastomeric impression materials are dispensed as:
opts: Two-component systems of a base and a catalyst
mcqs.explain: Polymerization and/or cross-linking then occurs by either a condensation or an addition reaction.

mcqs.q: Which is the key difference between a condensation and an addition reaction?
opts: The condensation reaction eliminates a small by-product molecule; the addition reaction does not
The addition reaction requires heat; the condensation reaction does not
The condensation reaction needs a platinum catalyst; the addition reaction needs tin
The addition reaction is reversible; the condensation reaction is not
mcqs.explain: The by-product is why condensation materials shrink more and are less dimensionally stable.

mcqs.q: Which pair of materials sets by an ADDITION reaction?
mcqs.explain: Polysulfide and condensation silicone are the two condensation-reaction materials, releasing water and ethyl alcohol respectively.

mcqs.q: Classification of elastomers by VISCOSITY gives four types. Which is the thickest?
mcqs.explain: The four, from thinnest to thickest, are light/syringe, regular/medium, heavy/tray and very heavy/putty.

mcqs.q: 'Syringe consistency' is another name for which viscosity?
mcqs.explain: It is thin enough to be injected around the preparation through a syringe tip.

mcqs.q: Polysulfide rubber is also known as:
mcqs.explain: Polyvinyl siloxane is the addition silicone and RTV refers to the condensation silicone.

mcqs.q: Which property is UNIQUELY high in polysulfide among the elastomers?
mcqs.explain: All three of the other elastomers are listed as having low tear strength.

mcqs.q: The by-product of the polysulfide setting reaction is:
mcqs.explain: Ethyl alcohol is the by-product of the condensation silicone reaction; addition silicones and polyethers release nothing.

mcqs.q: Because of its by-product, a polysulfide impression should be poured:
opts: Within 1 hour, to minimize dimensional changes
At any time, as it is dimensionally stable
mcqs.explain: Condensation silicone carries the same one-hour rule, for the same reason.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a stated disadvantage of polysulfide?
mcqs.explain: Polysulfide's tear strength is HIGH — that is one of its principal advantages.

mcqs.q: The catalyst paste of polysulfide contains:
mcqs.explain: Those other three belong to condensation silicone, addition silicone and polyether respectively.

mcqs.q: The base paste of polysulfide contains the prepolymer together with:
mcqs.explain: Dibutyl phthalate appears in both the base and the catalyst pastes of polysulfide.

mcqs.q: Condensation silicones are called RTV silicones because:
opts: Their polymer chains undergo catalyst-induced cross-linking at room temperature
They must be stored at room temperature
They are vulcanized in the laboratory oven
They set faster at mouth temperature than at room temperature
mcqs.explain: RTV stands for room temperature vulcanization.

mcqs.q: The by-product of the condensation silicone reaction is:
mcqs.explain: Its subsequent evaporation accounts for much of the shrinkage that occurs on setting.

mcqs.q: Why must STOCK TRAYS not be used with condensation silicones?
opts: Alcohol evaporation causes shrinkage — large and unpredictable in a thick bulk
Stock trays are simply not rigid enough for silicone
Silicone does not adhere to metal stock trays at all
Stock trays make the material set far too quickly
mcqs.explain: A custom tray holds a thin, uniform layer, so whatever shrinkage occurs is small and even.

mcqs.q: Condensation silicone is available in which consistencies?
opts: Extra light, light, medium, monophase, heavy and putty
mcqs.explain: Addition silicone has the six-viscosity range; polyether has low/medium/heavy; polysulfide has low/medium/high.

mcqs.q: The catalyst of condensation silicone contains:
mcqs.explain: The base paste is polydimethyl siloxane with fillers.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an advantage of condensation silicone?
mcqs.explain: It is hydrophobic, has low tear strength and shrinks on storage — those are all listed disadvantages.

mcqs.q: Addition silicones are commonly referred to as:
mcqs.explain: Mercaptan, Thiokol and RTV all refer to the older materials.

mcqs.q: Which material is described as the MOST HIGHLY ELASTIC of those currently available?
mcqs.explain: It shows virtually negligible distortion upon removal from undercuts.

mcqs.q: Which property of addition silicone allows the cast to be poured long after the impression is taken?
opts: Its dimensional stability, since no by-product is released
mcqs.explain: The addition reaction eliminates no small molecule, so there is no evaporation-driven shrinkage.

mcqs.q: Addition silicones make excellent materials for:
opts: Preliminary edentulous impressions in a stock tray
Interocclusal records only in edentulous patients
mcqs.explain: Border molding of special trays is the stated use of polyether.

mcqs.q: The MAIN disadvantage of silicones, both condensation and addition, is their:
mcqs.explain: The wettability of an impression material is regarded as one of the most important properties for clinical success.

mcqs.q: Moisture in the gingival sulcus is a problem because it:
opts: Prevents capturing the surface detail of a preparation
Causes the impression to adhere to the tooth
mcqs.explain: The material cannot wet and flow over a wet surface, so the finish line is left unrecorded.

mcqs.q: In the wetting diagram, the material with SUPERIOR wetting is the one that:
opts: Spreads out with a SMALL contact angle
Beads up with a LARGE contact angle
Forms a perfect hemisphere on the surface
Does not contact the surface at all
mcqs.explain: A small contact angle means the liquid spreads over the surface rather than pulling away from it.

mcqs.q: Addition silicone is supplied in how many viscosities?
opts: Six — extra light, light, medium, monophase, heavy and putty
Four — light, regular, heavy and putty
mcqs.explain: This is the widest range of any elastomer.

mcqs.q: The catalyst paste of ADDITION silicone contains:
opts: Dimethylsiloxane polymer, fillers and a platinum catalyst
mcqs.explain: The base paste is polymethylhydrosiloxane with fillers.

mcqs.q: Which elastomer is HYDROPHILIC?
mcqs.explain: Its affinity to water allows it to flow onto hydrated intraoral surfaces.

mcqs.q: Compared with addition silicones, polyether is:
opts: Cast with gypsum products more easily
Less accurate in reproducing anatomic details
mcqs.explain: Its hydrophilicity means the gypsum slurry wets the impression surface readily.

mcqs.q: Polyether is supplied in which viscosities?
mcqs.explain: Polysulfide uses the term 'high' rather than 'heavy' for its third consistency.

mcqs.q: The catalyst paste of polyether contains:
mcqs.explain: The base paste contains the polyether prepolymer with fillers and plasticizers.

mcqs.q: Polyether SWELLS in disinfectants and moist environments. The practical consequence is that it:
opts: Must be immersed with caution for a short exposure time of less than 10 minutes
Must be disinfected by spraying only
Should be immersed for at least 30 minutes
mcqs.explain: Chlorine compounds or iodophor are recommended, specifically because of their short exposure times.

mcqs.q: Why is polyether difficult to remove from the mouth?
opts: It is stiff, having good resistance to deformation
It sets with a strong exothermic reaction
It is hydrophilic and sticks to moist tissue
mcqs.explain: That same stiffness, combined with forced removal past undercuts, is what produces its high permanent deformation.

mcqs.q: Which material has BOTH good resistance to deformation AND high permanent deformation?
mcqs.explain: It is stiff in function but deforms permanently when forced out of undercuts.

mcqs.q: In hand mixing, the base and catalyst are dispensed as:
opts: Equal LENGTHS on a paper pad
Equal WEIGHTS on a glass slab
Equal VOLUMES in a rubber bowl
mcqs.explain: The tube orifices are sized so that equal lengths give the correct proportion.

mcqs.q: The correct hand-mixing sequence is:
opts: Initial mixing with a circular motion, then final mixing with broad strokes of the spatula
Initial mixing with broad strokes, then final mixing with a circular motion
mcqs.explain: The broad strokes at the end are what eliminate the streaks.

mcqs.q: Hand mixing is readily accomplished within:
mcqs.explain: A longer mix would consume too much of the available working time.

mcqs.q: Which materials are available for HAND mixing?
opts: All 4 types of elastomeric impression materials
mcqs.explain: Within hand mixing, the putty variation is limited to addition and condensation silicones.

mcqs.q: In the putty variation of hand mixing, the material is:
opts: Dispensed with manufacturer's scoops and kneaded with the fingers until free from streaks
Dispensed by weight and mixed with a stiff spatula
Mixed in a vacuum mixing machine
mcqs.explain: Addition and condensation silicones are the two putty systems available for this method.

mcqs.q: In the STATIC automixing system, the two components are mixed by:
opts: Being folded over each other many times as they pass through a STATIONARY internal spiral
mcqs.explain: The spiral does not move; the mixing comes entirely from the material being forced through it.

mcqs.q: The plungers of a static automixing gun are advanced by:
mcqs.explain: The ratchet ensures equal quantities of base and catalyst are extruded with each squeeze.

mcqs.q: A key advantage of automixing systems over hand mixing is that:
opts: They produce mixes with many fewer voids
They allow a longer working time
They are suitable for all four elastomers
They do not require a mixing tip
mcqs.explain: Polysulfide is in fact NOT available for static automixing — only addition silicones, condensation silicones and polyethers are.

mcqs.q: Which materials are available for STATIC AUTOMIXING?
opts: Addition silicones, condensation silicones and polyethers
mcqs.explain: Polysulfide is the one excluded from this system.

mcqs.q: In DYNAMIC MECHANICAL mixing, the base and catalyst are supplied in:
opts: Large collapsible plastic bags housed in a cartridge
Twin rigid cylinders in a plastic cartridge
mcqs.explain: Parallel plungers push against the bags, opening them and forcing the material into the mixing tip.

mcqs.q: How does the dynamic mechanical mixing tip DIFFER from the static automixing tip?
opts: Its internal spiral is motor driven, so it rotates
It contains no internal spiral at all
mcqs.explain: Mixing is therefore accomplished by rotation PLUS the forward motion of the material through the spiral.

mcqs.q: A specific advantage of dynamic mechanical mixing is that:
opts: Higher viscosity materials can be mixed with ease
It is the cheapest of the three systems
It works with all four elastomers
It eliminates the need for a tray adhesive
mcqs.explain: Its stated advantages are ease of use, speed and thoroughness of mixing.

mcqs.q: Which materials are available for DYNAMIC MECHANICAL mixing?
mcqs.explain: This is the newest and most restricted of the three systems.

mcqs.q: Which elastomer is specifically used for BORDER MOLDING of special trays?
mcqs.explain: Its stiffness and hydrophilicity suit it to recording the functional depth and width of the sulcus.

mcqs.q: Polysulfide, addition silicone and condensation silicone may all be disinfected by immersion in:
mcqs.explain: Polyether is the exception, restricted to chlorine compounds or iodophor for under 10 minutes.

mcqs.q: For the three immersion-tolerant elastomers, disinfectants requiring what exposure time are NOT recommended?
mcqs.explain: Prolonged immersion risks dimensional change even in the more tolerant materials.

saqs.q: Classify impression materials fully, giving the elastic and rigid groups.
saqs.a: ELASTIC — hydrocolloids: reversible (agar), irreversible (alginate); elastomers: polysulfide, polyether, addition silicone, condensation silicone. RIGID — impression plaster, impression wax, impression compound, zinc oxide eugenol.

Materials

impression plaster · impression wax · impression compound · zinc oxide eugenol

saqs.q: Classify impression materials by setting mechanism and use.
saqs.a: CHEMICAL (irreversible, thermoset) — rigid: plaster and ZOE, for edentulous ridges and interocclusal records; elastic: alginate and the non-aqueous elastomers, for teeth and soft tissues. PHYSICAL (reversible, thermoplastic) — rigid: compound and wax, for preliminary edentulous impressions; elastic: agar, for teeth and soft tissues.

Rigid
Elastic

alginate and the non-aqueous elastomers (polysulfide, polyether, condensation and addition silicone) — teeth and soft tissues
impression compound and wax — preliminary impressions of edentulous ridges

saqs.q: Explain the molecular basis of elasticity in elastomeric impression materials.
saqs.a: They contain molecules with weak interaction, tied at CROSS-LINK (tie) points into a three-dimensional network. The chains UNCOIL on stretching and SNAP BACK to their relaxed entangled state when the stress is removed. Covered by ADA Specification No. 19; also called non-aqueous elastomeric dental impression materials.

ans.text: They contain molecules with weak interaction between them, tied together at cross-link (tie) points to form a three-dimensional network. The chains uncoil on stretching and snap back to their relaxed, entangled state when the stress is removed. Covered by ADA Specification No. 19, and also known as non-aqueous elastomeric dental impression materials.

saqs.q: Give both classifications of the elastomers, by chemistry and by viscosity.
saqs.a: BY CHEMISTRY — polysulfide, condensation silicone, addition silicone, polyether. BY VISCOSITY — light body (syringe), regular/medium body, heavy body (tray), very heavy (putty).

saqs.q: Compare the condensation and addition reactions.
saqs.a: CONDENSATION — cross-linking WITH elimination of a small by-product molecule (water or alcohol), which causes shrinkage and affects dimensional stability; polysulfide and C-silicone. ADDITION — cross-linking WITHOUT any small molecule, so shrinkage is minimal and stability better; addition silicone (PVS) and polyether.

ADDITION

the by-product causes shrinkage and affects dimensional stability
no by-product, so shrinkage is minimal and dimensional stability better

saqs.q: Describe polysulfide rubber — its other names, properties, composition and the reason for its one-hour pouring rule.
saqs.a: The first elastomer (1950), also MERCAPTAN or THIOKOL. Excellent detail, long working time, good flexibility, high tear strength. Hydrophobic (dry the tissues), messy, stains clothes, offensive odour. BASE — polysulfide prepolymer, dibutyl phthalate, fillers; CATALYST — lead dioxide, sulfur, dibutyl phthalate. Low, medium and high consistencies, 2-paste. WATER is the by-product, so pour within an hour.

ans.text: The first elastomeric impression material (1950), also known as MERCAPTAN or THIOKOL.

rows: excellent detail reproduction · long working time · good flexibility · high tear strength. Hydrophobic — the tissues must be dried; messy, stains clothes, offensive odour

a 2-paste system in low, medium and high consistencies

saqs.q: List the advantages and disadvantages of polysulfide.
saqs.a: ADVANTAGES — good wettability, good surface detail, easy to remove, high tear strength. DISADVANTAGES — high permanent deformation, unpleasant taste and odour, pouring cannot be delayed beyond 1 hour, long setting time, care needed when disinfecting.

Disadvantages

saqs.q: Why are condensation silicones called RTV silicones, and why must stock trays not be used with them?
saqs.a: RTV = room temperature vulcanization — the polymer chains cross-link at room temperature under the catalyst. ETHYL ALCOHOL is the by-product, and its evaporation accounts for much of the setting shrinkage. A stock tray holds a thick, uneven bulk whose shrinkage is large and unpredictable in direction; a custom tray holds a thin, uniform layer so shrinkage is small and even.

ans.text: RTV = room temperature vulcanization — the polymer chains undergo catalyst-induced cross-linking at room temperature, forming an elastic silicone network.
ETHYL ALCOHOL is a by-product of the condensation reaction, and its evaporation accounts for much of the shrinkage on setting.

saqs.q: Give the composition, presentation, advantages and disadvantages of condensation silicone.
saqs.a: PRESENTATION — 2-paste (base and catalyst), or base paste with a low-viscosity liquid catalyst; light and putty consistencies. BASE — polydimethyl siloxane and fillers; CATALYST — stannous octoate and orthoethyl silicate. ADVANTAGES — good surface detail, good accuracy, low permanent deformation, easy to disinfect, highly acceptable. DISADVANTAGES — hydrophobic, shrinks on storage, pour within 1 hour, low tear strength.

saqs.q: Describe addition silicone, including its other name, its outstanding properties and its composition.
saqs.a: Also POLYVINYL SILOXANE (PVS). The most highly ELASTIC material available, with negligible distortion on removal from undercuts, exceptional accuracy, and dimensional stability allowing pouring long afterwards; also an excellent occlusal registration material. PRESENTATION — 2-paste in extra light, light, medium, monophase, heavy and putty. BASE — polymethylhydrosiloxane and fillers; CATALYST — dimethylsiloxane polymer, fillers and a PLATINUM catalyst.

ans.text: Commonly called POLYVINYL SILOXANE (PVS). The most highly elastic of the currently available materials, with virtually negligible distortion on removal from undercuts, exceptional accuracy in reproducing anatomic detail, and dimensional stability allowing pouring long after the impression. Also excellent for occlusal record registration.

rows: a 2-paste system — extra light, light, medium, monophase, heavy and putty viscosities

base — polymethylhydrosiloxane and fillers.
catalyst — dimethylsiloxane polymer, fillers and a platinum catalyst

saqs.q: Discuss the hydrophobicity of the silicones and the clinical importance of wettability.
saqs.a: A main disadvantage of silicones is their HYDROPHOBIC nature. Wettability is one of the most important properties for clinical success: a well-wetting material spreads with a SMALL contact angle, a poorly wetting one beads up with a LARGE contact angle. Moisture in the sulcus prevents capture of the preparation's surface detail — the material stops short of the sulcus depth and leaves the finish line unrecorded.

saqs.a: ADVANTAGES — good surface detail, good dimensional accuracy, good storage stability, low permanent deformation, a wide range of viscosities, easy to disinfect, highly acceptable. DISADVANTAGES — hydrophobic, low tear strength.

saqs.q: Describe polyether, including its distinguishing property, composition, and advantages and disadvantages.
saqs.a: Polyether has a high degree of WETTABILITY — its affinity to water lets it flow onto hydrated surfaces, and it casts with gypsum more easily than addition silicones. PRESENTATION — 2-paste in low, medium and heavy. BASE — polyether prepolymer, fillers, plasticizers; CATALYST — dichlorobenzene sulfonate, fillers, plasticizers. ADVANTAGES — hydrophilic, good detail, good accuracy, good resistance to deformation, acceptable. DISADVANTAGES — high permanent deformation, swells in disinfectants and moisture, difficult to remove, low tear strength.

saqs.q: Describe hand mixing of elastomeric impression materials, including the putty variation.
saqs.a: Equal LENGTHS of catalyst and base on a paper pad; initial mixing with a circular motion, final mixing with broad spatula strokes until streak-free — within 45 seconds. With a liquid catalyst, a specified number of drops per unit length. ALL FOUR elastomers can be hand mixed. PUTTY — manufacturer's scoops, kneaded with the fingers until streak-free; addition and condensation silicones only.

ans.text: Where the catalyst is a liquid, a specified number of drops per unit length is taken and mixing proceeds as for the 2-paste system. All four types of elastomer are available for mixing this way.
The putty variation — scoops supplied by the manufacturer for dispensing, kneaded with the fingers until free from streaks. Addition and condensation silicones are available for this method.

saqs.q: Describe static automixing and state which materials are available for it.
saqs.a: Base and catalyst sit in separate cylinders of a plastic cartridge, placed in a mixing gun whose two plungers advance by ratchet to extrude equal quantities. They are forced through a static-mixing tip containing a STATIONARY internal spiral, folding the two over each other many times to give a uniform mix at the tip. Extruded into a syringe or the tray. Gives far fewer voids than hand mixing. Addition silicones, condensation silicones and polyethers.

Extruded directly into an injection syringe or the impression tray

ans.text: Automixing gives many fewer voids than hand mixing. Available for addition silicones, condensation silicones and polyethers.

saqs.q: Describe dynamic mechanical mixing and how it differs from static automixing.
saqs.a: The third and newest system. Base and catalyst are in large plastic bags in a cartridge inserted into the top of a mixing machine, with a new tip on the front. Pressing the button drives parallel plungers against the collapsible bags, forcing material into the dynamic mixing tip. It differs in that the INTERNAL SPIRAL IS MOTOR DRIVEN and rotates — mixing by rotation PLUS forward motion. Ensures thorough mixing and handles higher viscosities. Advantages: ease, speed, thoroughness. Polyether and addition silicone.

saqs.q: List the uses of elastomeric impression materials.
saqs.a: Impressions of edentulous mouths for complete dentures · dentulous mouths for RPDs · prepared teeth for FPDs · bite registration · polyether specifically for border molding of special trays.

saqs.q: Tabulate the disinfection protocol for the four elastomers.
saqs.a: POLYSULFIDE, ADDITION and CONDENSATION SILICONE — immersion; glutaraldehyde, chlorine compounds or iodophor; disinfectants needing more than 30 minutes are not recommended. POLYETHER — immerse WITH CAUTION, under 10 minutes; chlorine compounds or iodophor; short exposure to avoid distortion. Polyether is the exception because it is hydrophilic and swells in disinfectants and moisture.
